company.name: Atlanta Electricals Ltd
company.about: Atlanta Electricals makes power transformers up to 220 kV (400 kV approved at its Vadod plant), distribution transformers, inverter-duty transformers for solar and wind projects, and special-purpose units. Its main customers are state transmission utilities, renewable power producers and EPC contractors in India, with exports at an early stage. It has five plants in Gujarat and Karnataka with about 63,000 MVA of capacity. It is not related to Atlantaa Ltd (ATLANTAA).

events.title: Stock jumps 7% intraday on peer TARIL's results, then falls 5% the next day to ₹1,711
events.details: After peer Transformers & Rectifiers reported September-quarter revenue up 61% and profit up 135%, Atlanta Electricals shares rose as much as 7.06% to ₹1,969.70 on 14 October 2026 but reversed to close at ₹1,802.20, down 2.69%. On 15 October they fell 5.05% to ₹1,711.30 as transformer stocks sold off, and closed at ₹1,695.20 on 16 October, about 8.5% below the 13 October close and below the 50-day average. No company news was found.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: with promoters holding 87%, the small free float makes the stock swing sharply on sector news ahead of its own results.

events.title: LME copper trades near its record at about US$14,400–14,700 a tonne, pressuring transformer costs
events.details: Copper on the London Metal Exchange traded at about US$14,436–14,741 a tonne in mid-October 2026, close to the record of about US$14,875 set on 10 September. Copper windings and CRGO electrical steel are the largest cost items in a transformer. Atlanta Electricals' Q1 FY27 margin dipped because of a lag in passing on raw-material costs, and its chairman said in August that he expected both metals to stay under upward pressure.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: fixed-price utility orders mean high copper prices can squeeze margins until contracts reprice.

events.title: 38th AGM passes all resolutions, including an ESOS of up to 7.7 lakh options (about 1%)
events.details: Shareholders at the 38th annual general meeting on 21 September 2026 approved all resolutions, including the ESOS 2026 employee stock option scheme of up to 7.7 lakh options, about 1% of equity. The FY26 annual report showed the company with no term-loan debt. Two days later, on 23 September, JP Morgan organised a plant visit for investors and analysts. The company closed its trading window from 1 October ahead of its Q2 results.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the option scheme causes only minor dilution; institutional interest is building from a low base.

events.title: Receives ₹194 Cr letter of intent from APTRANSCO for 12 large auto transformers
events.details: Atlanta Electricals received a letter of intent worth ₹193.92 crore from Transmission Corporation of Andhra Pradesh for 12 units of 160 MVA, 220/132 kV auto transformers. It added another state utility to a customer list that already included Gujarat, Karnataka, Punjab and Rajasthan transmission companies. The order is about 10% of FY26 revenue. It followed record order inflow of ₹972 crore in the June quarter.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a steady flow of state-utility orders of ₹190–300 crore each keeps the order book growing, though it also concentrates exposure to state utilities' payment cycles.

events.title: South Bihar discom withdraws its two-year debarment of the company
events.details: South Bihar Power Distribution Company withdrew a two-year debarment it had imposed on Atlanta Electricals in April or May 2026 over a legacy order worth less than ₹3 crore. The withdrawal restored the company's eligibility to bid for that utility's tenders. The underlying order was small relative to the business, and the company's main customers are other state transmission utilities.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the withdrawal removed a reputational overhang; the commercial impact was always small.

events.title: Q1 call: FY27 margin seen at 17–18%, about ₹2,400 Cr executable; 765 kV output targeted for Q4 FY27
events.details: On the Q1 FY27 call, management said growth was driven by volume, with no material change in prices or mix, and that the margin dip came from a lag in passing on raw-material costs. Reports put FY27 margin expectations at 17–18%, below the 18–20% guided in May, with about ₹2,400 crore of orders executable this year. Inverter-duty transformers were about 14% of revenue; a new plant for them is due by year-end, and commercial 765 kV production is targeted for the March 2027 quarter. Motilal Oswal kept its Buy rating and ₹1,950 target.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the softer margin outlook explains the post-results sell-off, while the 765 kV plan is the next step up in product mix.

events.title: Q1 FY27: revenue up 48% to ₹466 Cr, PAT up 50% to ₹47 Cr; record ₹972 Cr inflow, but stock hits lower circuit
events.details: For the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 48% year on year to ₹466.3 crore, EBITDA was ₹77.1 crore and profit after tax rose 50% to ₹46.8 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 16.5% from 20.0% in the March quarter. Order inflow was a record ₹972.4 crore, including ₹291.68 crore from Rajasthan's transmission utility and ₹285.15 crore from Punjab's, taking the order book to ₹3,116.6 crore, more than half of it 220 kV and above. The subsidiary Atlanta Trafo made a small loss. The shares hit their 5% lower circuit.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: strong orders and growth, but the market punished the margin drop at a valuation of about 60 times earnings.

events.title: Government lets four China-linked power-equipment makers bid for Indian tenders; grid stocks fall
events.details: A Finance Ministry order dated 24 June 2026, reported on 3 July, allowed four China-linked power-equipment firms, including TBEA and Nanjing Electric India, to bid for key Indian power projects for two years. Indian grid-equipment stocks fell 7–8% in the following weeks on worries about price competition in transformer tenders. Separately, India opened an anti-dumping investigation into imports of CRGO electrical steel, a key transformer input, in June.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: more bidders could pressure prices in state-utility tenders, while possible duties on CRGO steel could raise Atlanta's input costs.

events.title: Wins ₹285 Cr order from Punjab's PSTCL for 23 transformers; stock hits a record near ₹2,150
events.details: Atlanta Electricals won an order worth ₹285.15 crore from Punjab State Transmission Corporation for 23 power transformers of 160 MVA. The shares had set an all-time high of ₹2,067.45 on 1 June and went on to a peak of about ₹2,150 in early June, almost three times the ₹754 IPO price. In April the company had also received Power Grid Corporation's approval to supply transformers up to 400 kV from its Vadod plant, subject to a short-circuit test.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the early-June peak remains the high; the stock fell back after China-linked bidders were allowed into Indian tenders.

events.title: FY26: revenue up 49% to ₹1,852 Cr, PAT up 70% to ₹202 Cr; debt-free; Q4 profit more than doubles
events.details: FY26 consolidated revenue rose 48.8% to ₹1,851.5 crore, EBITDA rose 77.9% to ₹344.4 crore, an 18.6% margin, and profit after tax rose 70.1% to ₹201.8 crore. The March quarter was the strongest yet, with revenue of ₹747.6 crore, about 81% higher, a 20% margin and profit of ₹102.2 crore, more than double a year earlier. The company ended the year free of term debt with an order book of about ₹2,493 crore, guided for an 18–20% EBITDA margin in FY27 and approved an employee stock option plan. The shares hit the 5% upper circuit at ₹1,717.65.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the results showed the IPO-funded Vadod plant ramping up and set off the rally to the June record.

events.title: Motilal Oswal starts coverage of Atlanta Electricals with a Buy rating and ₹1,650 target
events.details: Motilal Oswal initiated coverage of several power-equipment makers, including Atlanta Electricals, CG Power and GE Vernova T&D India, on 21 April 2026, with a Buy rating and ₹1,650 target on Atlanta. It later raised the target to ₹1,950 and kept its Buy rating after the Q1 FY27 results. Motilal Oswal's investment-banking arm was also a lead manager for the company's 2025 IPO.

events.title: Wins five orders worth ₹288 Cr from Karnataka's KPTCL and an IPP building an NTPC project
events.details: Atlanta Electricals announced five transformer orders worth ₹288 crore in total. Two, worth about ₹146 crore, came from Karnataka Power Transmission Corporation for 13 transformers and 11 nitrogen-injection fire protection systems. The other three, worth about ₹142 crore, came from an independent power producer executing projects for NTPC. Further orders had lifted the order book to about ₹2,787 crore by then.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the orders widened the customer base beyond Gujarat and into renewable and central-utility projects.

events.title: Q3 FY26: revenue up 80% to ₹472 Cr, PAT nearly doubles to ₹43 Cr; record ₹2,451 Cr order book
events.details: For the December 2025 quarter, revenue rose 79.7% year on year to ₹472 crore, EBITDA was ₹91 crore at a 19.4% margin and profit after tax rose about 95% to ₹43 crore. The order book reached a record ₹2,451 crore after ₹796 crore of new orders, including the GETCO contract and a ₹134 crore order from Adani Green Energy for inverter-duty transformers. The shares closed 2.5% lower at about ₹940.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the first quarter in which the new Vadod plant clearly lifted growth, setting up the strong March quarter.

events.title: Wins ₹298 Cr of orders from Gujarat's GETCO for 25 power transformers
events.details: Atlanta Electricals received two orders worth ₹297.71 crore from Gujarat Energy Transmission Corporation for 25 transformers: twenty-one 220/66 kV, 160 MVA units, three 66/11.55 kV, 20 MVA units and one 220/132 kV, 150 MVA auto transformer. At the end of September 2025 the unexecuted order book had been about ₹2,069 crore. The order was equal to about a quarter of FY25 revenue.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: the largest order since listing, from the company's home-state utility, and the first of a run of ₹190–300 crore state-utility wins.

events.title: Q2 FY26: revenue up 17% to ₹317 Cr, but PAT dips 6% to ₹25 Cr in first results as a listed company
events.details: In its first quarterly results after listing, Atlanta Electricals reported September 2025 quarter revenue of ₹316.96 crore, up 17.3% year on year, and EBITDA of ₹54.8 crore, a 17.3% margin. Profit after tax fell about 6% to ₹25.3 crore. First-half revenue rose 10.9% to ₹632.07 crore. The order book stood at about ₹2,069 crore at the end of September. The new Vadod plant, which started in July 2025, was still ramping up.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a soft start, before the new capacity lifted growth sharply in the following two quarters.

events.title: Wins ₹116 Cr of orders, including its first major export contract worth about ₹20 Cr
events.details: Atlanta Electricals announced ₹116 crore of new transformer orders. They included its first major international contract, worth about US$2.3 million (₹20 crore), for two 63 MVA 132/33 kV and two 30 MVA 33/11 kV transformers for a buyer in Asia or the Middle East that was not named. Domestic orders worth ₹56 crore and ₹40 crore were for solar pooling substations in Rajasthan and Karnataka. Management targets exports at about 15% of revenue within three years.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: small in value, but a first step into export markets at a time of global transformer shortages.

events.title: CRISIL upgrades credit rating to A/Stable; shares jump 10% to a new high of ₹993
events.details: CRISIL Ratings upgraded Atlanta Electricals' long-term bank facilities to CRISIL A/Stable, with A1 for short-term facilities, two weeks after the IPO. The shares rose about 10% to a then record of ₹993.40. CRISIL reaffirmed the ratings in February 2026 on enhanced facilities of ₹1,460 crore. By March 2026 the company had borrowings of only about ₹3 crore, against an order book that had grown above ₹2,400 crore.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: a stronger rating supports bidding for large utility tenders, which need bank guarantees.

events.title: Lists at ₹857, a 13.7% premium to the ₹754 IPO price, after the issue was subscribed about 71 times
events.details: Atlanta Electricals' shares began trading on 29 September 2025 at ₹857 on NSE and ₹858.10 on BSE, about 13.7% above the ₹754 issue price. The ₹687 crore IPO, open from 22 to 24 September in a ₹718–754 band, comprised ₹400 crore of new shares and ₹287.34 crore sold by existing holders. It was subscribed about 70.6 times, with institutional demand at about 195 times. Promoters kept about 87% of the company.
events.why_it_matters: Pipeline assessment: strong demand but a very small free float, which is why the stock has moved so sharply since.
